witness_description: Take D = Q with its usual order. The bounded sweep finds 1/2 in D, while every g(n) is the integer rational n/1.
refutation_explanation: The exact rational 1/2 cannot equal g(n)=n·1_Q for any integer n, because every such image has reduced denominator 1 whereas 1/2 has reduced denominator 2. Thus g: Z → Q is not onto, and Q is an ordered integral domain.
search_space: All 10 numerator-denominator pairs (p,q) with p visited in the fixed order (0,1,-1,2,-2) and q visited in the fixed order (1,2), interpreted exactly as Fraction(p,q); the entire bounded space is swept.
